visual.general_description: Two framed groups of grayscale axial head MRI slices, labelled A and B, each with two slices.
visual.detailed_description: The figure is a single 667 x 192 pixel grayscale image divided into two white-bordered frames on black backgrounds. Frame A (left) and frame B (right) each contain two axial MRI slices of the head at the level of the temporal lobes, brainstem and posterior fossa, anterior at top, with orbits visible in one slice per frame. A white circle with a black letter A or B is at the lower right of each frame. No arrows, graphs, tables, scale bars or readable text beyond the letters are present; tiny unreadable specks lie at the top edge of each slice.

panels.general_description: Panel A: two side-by-side grayscale axial MRI slices of the head at the level of the temporal lobes, with a white circular letter A at lower right.
panels.detailed_description: Two axial head MRI slices sit side by side in a black-background frame, anterior at top. In the left slice both orbits with dark globes and the nasal/ethmoid region are visible anteriorly; the temporal lobes lie to each side of a midline brainstem/interpeduncular region, with occipital lobes posteriorly. The right slice is at a similar level without the globes, showing frontal base, temporal lobes, brainstem and cerebellar vermis region posteriorly. Cortex and white matter are moderately bright and CSF spaces are dark; no focal mass, arrow or marker is annotated. A white circle containing a black letter A is at the lower right of the second slice. Hippocampal signal changes described in the caption are not distinguishable on this small image.
